title: Physical quantities and units

parts.text:
1
A sheet of gold leaf has a thickness of 0.125 µm. A gold atom has a radius of 174 pm.
Approximately how many layers of atoms are there in the sheet?
A
4
B
7
C
400
D
700

hints: Notice the thickness is $0.125 \, \mu\text{m}$ but the atom size is given as a radius of $174 \, \text{pm}$ - convert both to the same unit such as metres or picometres.
Recall that one atomic layer stacked through the thickness contributes a full diameter $2r$, not just one radius $r$.
Divide the total sheet thickness by the thickness of one atom $2 \times 174 \, \text{pm}$ and round to the nearest order given in the options.
walkthrough: Convert both lengths to metres. Thickness $t = 0.125 \, \mu\text{m} = 0.125 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m} = 1.25 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
Find the thickness of one layer. One atom contributes its diameter: $d = 2r = 2 \times 174 \, \text{pm} = 348 \, \text{pm} = 3.48 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$.
Set number of layers $N = t/d$ because the layers stack to make the total thickness.
Approximately $360$ is closest to $400$ given the options. This is option C

A.explanation: About 4 would result from ignoring the $10^6$ difference between $\mu\text{m}$ and pm and from using radius instead of diameter.

B.explanation: About 7 would result from dividing $0.125$ by $174$ without converting $\mu\text{m}$ to pm and correcting for diameter.

C.explanation: Thickness $1.25 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ divided by atom diameter $3.48 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$ gives about $360$, approximately $400$.

D.explanation: About 700 would result from dividing by the atomic radius $174 \text{ pm}$ instead of the diameter $348 \text{ pm}$ that makes one layer.
